title: Metallurgy & extraction principles
examples: What is the difference between roasting and smelting?
Can you explain how concentration helps us?
What is the role of carbon in the reduction process?

explain.say: Today we will learn about getting metals from ores. First we must concentrate the ore material.
Concentration separates the valuable mineral from the useless rock. We use methods like gravity separation for this.
Roasting involves heating the ore in the presence of excess air. This process changes the chemical form of the metal.
Reduction is the process of removing oxygen from the metal oxide. This is often done using carbon or hydrogen.

draw.text: Reduction: Metal Oxide + C $\rightarrow$ Metal + CO

explain.say: Refining purifies the crude metal obtained after reduction. Electrolytic refining is a common method to achieve high purity.
In everyday life, extracting aluminum from bauxite ore uses electrolysis. This is a large industrial example of refining.

faq.q: What is the main difference between roasting and smelting?
faq.a: Roasting specifically involves heating the ore with air to form an oxide. Smelting is a broader term for reducing the ore, often using coke.
asks: When do I use air in the process?
Is smelting always done with coke?

faq.q: Why do we need to concentrate the ore first?
faq.a: Concentration removes the unwanted rock, called gangue. This makes the subsequent chemical processes much more efficient and cheaper.

faq.q: What is the role of carbon in reduction?
faq.a: Carbon acts as a reducing agent. It has a higher affinity for oxygen than the metal we want to recover.
asks: What happens if there is not enough carbon?

faq.q: Is refining always done using electricity?
faq.a: No, refining can involve multiple steps. Electrolytic refining uses electricity, but other chemical methods also exist.
asks: What is the goal of refining?
What is the purest form of metal?

faq.q: Which process is used for iron ore?
faq.a: Iron ore is usually roasted or smelted first, followed by reduction using coke in a blast furnace.
asks: Does the process for copper differ from iron?
What is the final product after iron extraction?

facts: Concentration separates valuable minerals from waste rock called gangue.
Roasting heats ores with air to form metal oxides.
Reduction involves removing oxygen from the metal oxide, often with carbon.
Refining purifies the crude metal to a very high standard.
Electrolysis is a common technique used during the refining stage.

quiz.say: An ore containing copper sulfide is heated strongly with air. Which process is this?
quiz.why: Roasting is the specific process of heating an ore with air to convert it into a more reactive oxide.

wrong.0: Refining happens after you have already obtained the crude metal.
wrong.1: Concentration only removes the useless rock, not changing the chemistry.
wrong.3: Reduction happens later when you remove oxygen from the oxide.

quiz.say: A chemist has a crude block of copper metal. To make it pure enough for wiring, what step must follow?
quiz.why: Refining is the final step dedicated entirely to increasing the purity of the metal.

wrong.1: Roasting is used on the original ore, not the already formed metal block.
wrong.2: Reduction is needed when the metal is still bound in an oxide.
wrong.3: Concentration deals with separating the ore from the surrounding rock.

quiz.say: If the ore is $\text{Fe}2\text{O}3$ and the reducing agent is carbon, what is the primary chemical reaction type?
quiz.why: The reaction removes oxygen from the iron oxide using carbon, which is the definition of reduction.

wrong.0: Concentration is a physical separation process, not a chemical reaction.
wrong.2: Roasting usually involves adding oxygen, not removing it.
wrong.3: Refining is a purification step, not the chemical reaction itself.
